labels.description: Tariffs and retaliatory counter measures are elevated into the headline, and the body adds proposed additional export controls and tariffs, limited access to rare earth minerals and other raw materials, tariff-driven cost, pricing, market access and planning impacts, and the cost and fines exposure of complying with rapidly changing trade restrictions, while dropping the limitation of sanctions to parties in certain conflict zones.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures are disclosed (rare earth and raw material access, tariff compliance cost and penalty risk), and under criterion 3 the scope of the sanctions and trade risk is widened; the 2024 to 2025 revenue-share date roll is routine with the 56 percent figure unchanged.

labels.description: The PFAS manufacturing exit moves from in progress ("is progressing toward the exit of all PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025") to completed ("completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025"), with new disclosure of ongoing water treatment, remediation and facility disposition obligations, third-party PFAS product use that will continue beyond 2025 with transitions not completed, the dropped 2018 State of Minnesota settlement example ($897 million pre-tax charge), and asset retirement obligations broadened to charges on ongoing asset use, retirement or disposition.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: a planned exit becomes realized and expected continuation of third-party PFAS use becomes certain; criterion 2 and 4 also apply because the Minnesota settlement and its $897 million figure are dropped and international litigation is newly referenced.

labels.description: The paragraph on artificial intelligence development, use and regulatory risk is removed and replaced by a new paragraph on risks as a direct and indirect supplier to the U.S. and other governments, covering procurement compliance, audit and contract termination rights, funding uncertainty, False Claims Act liability and suspension or debarment, with customers added to the parties whose conduct creates compliance risk.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed risk (artificial intelligence) is removed and a new exposure (government contracting) is disclosed; the customers addition also widens scope under criterion 3.
